title: Adaptive trace-sidecar and model-aware SLO triage
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight trace-sidecar that enriches incoming request telemetry with model/version/route context, performs adaptive span sampling, and forwards enriched spans and derived metrics to the observability pipeline for faster SLO attribution and anomaly triangulation. Goal: reduce mean time-to-detect and mean time-to-assign for model-level SLO regressions by providing pre-correlated signals (model_id, route_hash, input_shape, tail-latency-flag) before they hit downstream ingesters. Work spans runtime hooks, agent-side enrichment, metric/log bridge, and dashboard panels for model-aware latency/error slices. Priorities: 1) non-blocking sampling (minimal p95 overhead), 2) deterministic correlation keys for rollouts, 3) graceful fallback when sidecar is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar deployed to canary hosts with <1ms added p95 latency under synthetic load
Enriched spans include model_id, model_version, route, request_signature_hash, and kv_cache_hit boolean
Adaptive sampler reduces trace volume for healthy routes by 5-10x while preserving 99% of unique error-span signatures
Grafana dashboard shows model-level p50/p95/p99 latency and error-rate heatmap with drilldowns to trace links
Alerting rule: model-version burn-rate alert that triggers when error-burn > 1.5x baseline for 5m and has automated paging policy classification
comments: 2026-03-02 - Planning: synced with runtime team (Priya) about lightweight hook API; decided on a pull-based hook so runtime is not blocked by sidecar I/O.

2026-03-04 - Design review: frontend team asked for a stable correlation key for rollouts; agreed to use route_hash + model_version + 8-byte request_signature. Added to spec: deterministic hashing and salt rotation policy.

2026-03-06 - Engineering note: prototype sidecar using Rust + tokio on canary. Initial microbenchmark shows 0.6ms median overhead and 0.9ms p95 for 512B requests. Still investigating CPU tail when sampling alpha is high.

2026-03-08 - QA: end-to-end tests added that assert span enrichment and metric emission. Found issue where kv_cache_hit flag was missing for batched requests; added request-level iterator to runtime hook to surface per-subrequest cache results.
2026-03-10 - Security review: security requested that correlation keys are reversible only by service identity; implemented HMAC with team KMS and scoped envelope in the sidecar.

2026-03-12 - Ops/Runbook: drafted paging policy mapping. If a burn-rate alert ties to a single model-version and error-type, page model-owner oncall with high priority; otherwise page infra oncall. Added dampening window to avoid double-paging across model and infra teams.
2026-03-13 - PR feedback: infra asked to expose sampling controls via k8s configmap for faster tuning. Marcus created PR #6842 (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6842).
notes: Trade-offs considered: full-span forwarding vs enrichment+sampling. We chose enrichment+sampling to minimize egress cost and CPU on the ingest pipeline while keeping triage fidelity. Future: evaluate a hybrid mode that streams full spans for flagged requests only.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: sidecar prototype + hook API (canary) -> Phase 2: adaptive sampler + deterministic keys -> Phase 3: metric bridge and dashboard -> Phase 4: global rollout and alerting rules. Rollout will start with non-critical customer tenants, then Dedicated clusters, then host-wide.
